2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal in a nut shell can be stated thus that the present respondent No.1 as pre-emptor filed a Pre-emption Case being No. 08 of 2008 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Narsingdi against the present pre-emptee-appellant and others contending inter alia that the case land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.5 was recorded in the name of Abdul Aziz and Dud Meher, son of Sheikh Abbas. The S.A. Khatian No.7 was correctly prepared in the name of Abdul Aziz who died leaving behind one son the pre-emtor and three daughters the opposite parties namely, Majeda Begum @ Khodeja, Razia Khatun and Ambia Khatun. Ambia Khatun transferred her share in favour of the pre-emptor-petitioner. Subsequently, the opposite party Nos.2 and 3 behind that back of the pre-emptor-petitioner without giving him any notice transferred the case land in favour of opposite party No.1 collusively. The further case of the pre-emptor was such that some land from suit plot was acquired by C & B and the purchaser opposite party No.1 who is the pre-emptee to the original case is a stranger-purchaser. For getting the case land pre-epmteed the pre-emptor-respondent instituted the original pre-emption miscellaneous case under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951. 

 11. It is an admitted position that Abdul Aziz was the original owner of the land of the case plots and at his demise his one son and three daughters inherited the property. The learned Court below in his observation and findings arrived at a decision in consultation with the papers that on the basis of Exhibit-3 government acquired 62 decimals of land from suit plot No.37 in which the area of land was 92 decimals. The learned Court having gone through case kabala along with the connected khatians rightly arrived at a decision that the pre-emptor had a pre-emptable right and he rightly instituted the original case for getting the case land pre-empted on the basis of his co-sharership in the case holding. But it is curious to note from the impugned judgment and order that the learned Court below not at all discussed the evidence on records as adduced from the sides of the respective parties in support of their respective case on the point of controversy between them. In fact; excepting the statement of the OPW.1 on his application for withdrawal of the money; no evidence was considered or evaluated by the learned trial Court which were adduced from the sides of the parties during trial of the original case.
